I should clarify — I'm the routing layer, so my "choice" was just selecting which model handles your previous query. Here's the actual reasoning behind that routing decision:

1. **Task type**: Your request was an evidence-citation/extraction task — pulling supporting quotes from a text. That maps to the "Extraction & Retrieval" eval dimension.

2. **Capability comparison**: On extraction, Curlew (83.6) and Whimbrel (81.6) are within 2.0 points, so the docs say to treat that as a tie. I looked at other relevant signals: Curlew scores higher on IFEval (89.3 vs 85.6), which matters because your query has an explicit instruction-following demand ("Don't half-do it") — you want thorough, complete compliance.

3. **No moderation factor**: Whimbrel's main edge is handling harm-adjacent content without aversion. Your literary-analysis request has nothing sensitive in it, so that advantage was irrelevant.

So with the extraction scores effectively tied, Curlew's stronger instruction-following profile broke the tie — a good fit for a request that emphasizes doing the job completely.
